Subject: Cryptokey handling discussion and next actions

Hi Susan / Frank —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call + proposed next steps so we stay aligned on encryption and key custody requirements for the PoC: 

What we covered (short):
- At-rest encryption: Redwood uses AES-256 at rest; customer data buckets are encryption scoped per-tenant.
- In-transit: TLS 1.3 (mutual TLS available on Dedicated/Private).
- KMS options: Hosted-managed keys (Redwood KMS), customer-managed keys in cloud KMS (BYOK), and HSM-backed CMKs for Dedicated/Private.
- KV cache and tokenization concerns for model context: we explained prefix caching and selective masking.

Action items / asks for MediBridge: (please confirm by EOD Wed)
1) Which key custody model do you prefer for the PoC? Options: "Redwood-managed", "Customer KMS (BYOK)", or "HSM/CMK (on Dedicated)".
2) If BYOK: provide target cloud KMS provider (AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault / GCP KMS) and an initial key alias we can reference.
3) Please attach your latest SOC 2 report (or SOC 2 Type II bridge letter) and any HIPAA/GDPR controls documentation relevant to data residency.
4) Fill out the attached one-page encryption decision worksheet (I attached vendor-questionnaire-initial.xlsx) — Frank, Susan: a quick baseline helps us size the right deployment.

Tentative Redwood owners: Marissa (security intake + SOC review), Ben (deployment sizing / Dedicated options), me (commercial / timeline).

Next proposed milestones:
- This week: MediBridge confirms custody preference + uploads SOC2 (target Wed).
- Next week: Redwood security does a 30-min intake review and sends a short evidence checklist.
- Following: If BYOK, schedule a 1-hour KMS integration sync with infra (Ben + security).

If you prefer, we can accept SOC2 via secure upload link or sign an NDA — let me know.

Thanks — looking forward to the next steps.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

Alex —

Thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers from our side: 

1) For the PoC, we prefer Customer KMS (BYOK) so we can keep key rotation under our control.
2) Primary target: AWS KMS. I'll confirm the key alias this afternoon; Frank is provisioning it.
3) I'll upload our SOC 2 Type II redacted report to the Drive link you shared by EOD today. We also have a HIPAA overview and our DPA that I'll include.
4) We'll fill the worksheet and return it tomorrow.

A couple of clarifying questions from our security team: 
- Do you have a recommended approach for short-lived access to the KMS key for Redwood's infra? We assume an IAM-role-based granting pattern is best.
- For the HSM-backed CMK option, can you share expected lead time and minimum hardware commitment (if we evaluated Dedicated later)?

Thanks — Susan

Thanks for the heads up, Alex. I'll take the SOC2 when it arrives and run our intake checklist. Preliminary notes: 

- SOC2: we'll validate scope (storage, transmission, change mgmt) and look for any outstanding exceptions for 2027. If anything looks risky, we'll flag a short follow-up with MediBridge.
- Short-lived KMS access: recommend cross-account IAM roles + KMS key grants to a Redwood-AWS role with Get/Decrypt for limited scope. We'll suggest using AWS KMS Grant with a short TTL and CloudTrail alerts. I'll draft the one-pager for Ben to expand on the operational steps.
- HSM-backed Dedicated: rough estimate — procurement lead time 6–8 weeks for a Dedicated pool, minimum commitment equivalent to a 4-GPU unit for an initial throughput lane. I'll confirm exact SKU + pricing this week.

I'll prepare the evidence checklist and the KMS pattern doc and share both in the Drive link you included.
